rows.grounds: locative of loka, indicating the sphere of ordinary experience
ablative of anupapatti, expressing reason or cause
noun denoting authoritative means or result of knowing
compound: vyavahāra (practical-usage) + ga (going-reaching), describing what extends to ordinary practice

items.question: How do non-establishment in the world and practical usage support the claim of valid cognition?
premises: In the world, certain distinctions lack independent establishment.
Valid cognition is recognized within that same worldly sphere.
Practical usage operates effectively despite such non-establishment.
items.inference: Therefore, valid cognition and practical usage remain grounded even where independent establishment is absent.
uncertainties: The exact logical relation implied by the repeated ca particles is context-dependent.
vyavahāragā may qualify pramā or function as a parallel subject.
items.plain_english: And in the world, because of non-establishment, valid cognition and that which extends to practical usage also obtain.
